flush(): voidPublish the backend's current state (no-op for stream/socket backends that emit as you record). Long-lived servers driving a textfile backend MUST call this on a schedule — the file is only rewritten inside flush(), and nothing in the library arms a timer on the host's event loop.
register(Descriptor $descriptor): voidRegister a metric descriptor for early TYPE/HELP emission. Re-registering the identical (name, type, help, labelKeys) is a no-op; a SECOND, DIFFERENT descriptor for the same name throws — silently keeping the first would let a copy-pasted registration pin stale TYPE/HELP onto an evolving metric. labelKeys are compared in order (the DTO stores the list as given): a reordering is a different declaration and conflicts like any other change.

The pair reads the monotonic clock (hrtime()), not wall time: a system clock step (NTP correction, manual set) can never turn a duration negative in a finally arm that rethrows.

Util final class

Shared utility functions for the metrics library.

MethodSummary
static tagKey(array $tags): stringSort tags by key and build a stable, collision-free k=v|k2=v2 string. Every key and value is backslash-escaped first (\ → \\, | → \|, = → \=), so a separator that appears inside a tag payload cannot impersonate the pair delimiter: without it, ['x' => 'a|y=b'] and ['x' => 'a', 'y' => 'b'] would serialize identically and collapse two distinct series into one cardinality slot.
static nameToken(string $name): stringThe storage-key NAME segment gets the identical escape a tag token gets (see self::escapeTagToken()). In-memory accumulation accepts arbitrary raw names — there is no sanitize-name gate on that path — so without this the name 'x|y=1' would land in exactly the bucket 'x' + tags ['y' => '1'] folds into (finding 013). One escaper for every segment makes the separator unforgeable from both sides, and the map stays readable: a clean name escapes to itself, so the storage key of every well-behaved series is unchanged.
static nonFiniteToken(float $value): ?stringCanonical exposition spellings for non-finite readings.
static needsExponentForm(float $value): boolTrue when the fixed six-decimal rendering would lie: magnitudes beyond the integer-precision band print noise, and non-zero values below 1e-6 collapse to "0.000000" (a sub-microsecond timed() span reporting a zero sum). Exponent form keeps both honest.
static displaySafe(string $text): stringSweep terminal-control bytes out of a string that is about to be interpolated into an exception message. TUI hosts print throwable messages verbatim, and metric names/paths are operator- (or in the SSH middleware, attacker-) controlled — delegating to the shared sugar-core display sanitizer keeps the sweep consistent fleet-wide.

snapshot(): arrayStructured read surface (sugar-metrics-022): every accumulated series as its own row, with the internal storage key decoded back into the faithful name + tags the caller emitted. The raw maps above stay for zero-copy access, but they are keyed by the self::key() grammar — consumers parsing name|k=v by hand re-implement the escaper wrong exactly when a payload carries a separator (an adversar- ial name like 'x|y=1' is indistinguishable from a fold once you split naively), and histogram consumers re-implement the reservoir aggre- gation. Additive: no existing behavior moves.
histogramSummary(string $name, array $tags = []): ?arrayAggregate view of one histogram series, or null when the series is absent. count/sum/mean describe the RETAINED RESERVOIR (bounded at maxSamplesPerKey); observed is the total number of samples ever seen for the series, so post-cap the two axes are honestly distinct — a reservoir mean is not a stream mean, and pretending otherwise would just move the consumer-boilerplate problem inside the library.

flush(): void
remove(string $name, array $tags = []): voidDrop one accumulated series (name + label set) from the backend's in-memory state, plus its collision-detector records and family index entry. The storage key is derived exactly like the write path, so this reclaims what counter()/gauge()/histogram()/... stored — including the Registry's cardinality-eviction forward, which arrives with the merged tag set. The next flush() simply no longer emits the removed series; the textfile itself is rewritten whole on every flush, so no stale line survives. remove() consults the same collision record the write path keeps: a call whose raw (name, tags) is NOT the identity recorded under that folded key would reach through the fold and silently wipe an innocent twin, so it is refused exactly like a colliding write; the honest reclaim drops the record with the series, freeing the fold for the twin to claim later.
clear(): voidReset the backend: forget every accumulated series, dirty flag, collision record, family index entry, and registered descriptor. The next flush() writes an empty textfile (the file itself is not unlinked — deleting the target from under a watching node_exporter is a deployment decision, not a metrics-library one).
